Eli: Ran an nsys trace against the vLLM -> TensorRT hotpath on the repro. High-level: ~35% of GPU time attributed to a busy-wait in the wrapper/scheduler layer, ~30% in IExecutionContext::enqueue (TensorRT engine invoke), ~12% in cudaMemcpyAsync spikes (KV cache sync), rest in small kernels. Trace uploaded: https://internal-artifacts/runs/1795004321

Eli: Command used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace1795 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt python -m vllm.server --model t5-quant --batcher=custom
```

Priya: Can you paste the nsys "CUDA Activity" timeline snippet or a top table? Curious about cuLaunchKernel vs memcpy timings. Also: what seq lengths / batch distribution?

Eli: Pasted top summary from the trace (approx):
`wrapper_spin: 210ms (35%), trt_enqueue: 185ms (31%), cudaMemcpyAsync: 72ms (12%), small_kernels (attn, gelu): 60ms (10%), CPU-scheduler-spin: 45ms (7%)`

Jordan: If KV cache warmups map to the memcpy bursts that would explain tail latency spikes for cold prompts. Are memcpy bursts correlated with first token in a batch, or every request?

Eli: It's the first few tokens after context extension / cache miss. We see repeated host->device memcpys when the batcher merges late arrivals: short windows where 1-2 requests get merged trigger memcpy per request instead of coalesced region. Scheduler is spinning on a condition variable in the wrapper, polling every ~1-2ms which shows up as CPU/GPU overlap in the timeline.

perf-bot: Automated note: perf traces saved to s3://perf-traces/eng-runtime/1795004321/ (nsys + perfetto artifacts).

Priya: Short list of hypothesis/fixes: 1) Replace busy-spin with exponential backoff (sleep 50-200us) to cut CPU overhead and reduce host wakeups. 2) Aggregate KV cache writes into a single coalesced H2D when possible. 3) Pin host staging buffers and use cudaMemcpyAsync + streams tied to engine invoke. 4) Try cudaGraph capture for steady short sequences to eliminate enqueue overhead.

Jordan: I'll add NVTX ranges around the vLLM wrapper boundaries (before/after enqueue, before/after KV memcpy) and re-run perfetto so we can correlate exact timestamps. Will also instrument the scheduler loop counters.

Eli: Added one more: test removing the little-spin in the batcher where it does `while (!ready) { /* cpu pause */ }` — replace with `std::this_thread::sleep_for(50us)` as an A/B. If latency SLOs don't regress, we win.

Priya: Can someone run a quick A/B: current vs sleep-backoff on the same workload (seq length distribution attached). If we see drop in CPU-side wakeups and reduced memcpy fragmentation -> roll a small patch.

Jordan: I'll run nsys + perfetto with NVTX markers and post the new trace by EOD. Assign: Jordan (instrument + trace), Priya (prototype backoff), Eli (investigate KV coalescing).

Eli: Thanks — will follow up with the diff for the KV coalescing idea. :thumbsup:
